q: Now she will only behave that way with her dad. With me, it’s like she’s a screaming and crying balloon man from a car dealership flailing around and hanging off of me.
cx: 14-month-old changed after a nap transition and a holiday.

q: I hate seeing my happy baby so miserable. I miss feeling like I can connect with her through play. I am irrationally afraid that if she is too cranky, she’ll get kicked out of daycare.
cx: Child moves to full-time daycare next week.

q: We did the bare naked for 3 days method and there was a little defiance at first, but she was all but potty trained in two weeks.

q: This shit (pun intended) is exhausting. I had periods of higher accidents with her older brothers, but nothing like this. It’s like she totally forgot what we just spent the last half a year doing.

q: Is it really just summer and the change in schedule? Is she tired from starting to drop naps? What do I doooooo? I’m so frustrated by this sudden extreme backslide. I guess I just need a pep talk. 😬😭

q: He thinks pooping and peeing his pants and making us change it is funny. We have tried everything to show him that it’s yucky and he gets prizes for going in the potty. Nothing is working and we’ve been potty training for over a year.

q: We act very disappointed when he has to be changed. My theory is that he likes that he can predict what will happen when he has to be changed. Someone suggested staying very neutral and I think that might help.

q: Emotionless has been working well!!!! No need to have him clean up so far!
cx: Update twelve days later.

q: Having no reaction is working wonders so far!
cx: Same update.

q: I get to work 4-5 times a month, and I LOVE my job (paramedic). I would work more but childcare is $2000 a month full time.
cx: Mostly stay-at-home mother of a three- and four-year-old.

q: At least one wakes up almost every night and they demand me and will not accept my husband putting them back to sleep. I've been short and snappy and often get headaches now.
cx: Night wakings fall only to her.

q: My husband thinks I need to go to therapy. I've been to therapy for this before and it did absolutely nothing.
cx: What her husband suggests.

q: But this isn't a therapy problem. This is a "I need a goddamned break". Like a 4-5 day vacation by myself.
cx: What she believes she needs.

q: I feel guilty for being overstimulated. I feel like I'm drowning and half a tantrum away from a panic attack.
cx: Her state before school starts in August.

q:
She speaks sentences and can communicate her emotions well, so I thought potty training would be a bit easier for us. 

WRONG.
cx: Almost-three-year-old described as sensitive and strong-willed.

q: I bought her an incentive basket with just a bunch of Target dollar tree items. She wants the items but won’t go potty.

q: We have tried bribery and having prizes/toy box but shes top stubborn. Weve told her she can even ask us for a nappy and she can wear it to poop in the bathroom.

q: I am at my wits end with her hiding to do it and then noticing when shes sat down and squished it into the carpet, or the couch.

cx: Reply to a bottomless suggestion.

q: the problem is she takes 30-60 minutes to eat meals in her high chair and regularly pees during the longer dinner time meal. For those of you who normally use a high chair what did you do in those first focused potty training days where you’re supposed to watch them like a hawk?

q: How long did you do that for before offering a seat at the regular table? Did you have to wait until she reliably self initiated needing to use the potty?

q: I love being at work, I despise being at home. I dread the weekend as I have to spend time with her. I know that makes me sound horrendous but I just can’t enjoy any of it. The tantrums are non stop.

q: When I’m out with her I envy everyone. The people who can just go for a walk, go to the gym..socialise.
